title: The Week in Vulnerabilities: Toptech, Lantronix, Langflow, and CISA Malcolm Flaws
content_md: This Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs (CRIL) weekly vulnerability report covers two views of risk: what attackers tried against Cyble's global honeypot sensors, and what the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) disclosed for industrial control systems (ICS). The Cyble Global Sensor Intelligence (CGSI) network observed exploitation attempts against about 20 known vulnerabilities. They range from newly disclosed flaws in WordPress, Apache Solr, and Langflow to years-old bugs in GPON home routers and embedded TCP/IP stacks. On the industrial side, CISA issued 14 ICS advisories covering 54 vulnerabilities. Of these, 13 were rated critical, 18 high, 18 medium, and five low. Affected vendors include Toptech Systems, Lantronix, VIVOTEK, MikroTik, Armatura, Monta, Anjvision, and, unusually, CISA itself. Cyble sensors also recorded active malware campaigns, phishing emails, and brute-force attacks against internet-exposed services. Real-World Attacks Observed by Cyble Sensors Attackers moved quickly against newly disclosed flaws in web platforms and AI tooling, while older IoT and embedded-device bugs continued to draw steady traffic.
